description: A Raspberry Pi Pico family board with an RP2040 or RP2350 chip, 26 GPIO pins on two edge rows and a debug header, in Pico, Pico W, Pico 2 and Pico 2 W variants.
summary: The board runs the user's program in the iynk interpreter, in MicroPython or Arduino C++. Pins, PWM, I2C, serial and timing follow the pico board profile. It is not the RP2040 chip.
led: On-board LED on GP25. On the W boards the LED hangs off the radio chip; use Pin("LED").
gp23: Internal pin: sets the board's power-supply mode. Leave it alone.
gp24: Internal pin: tells whether USB power is present.
gp29: Internal pin: reads the supply voltage through a divider (VSYS divided by 3).

models.1: MicroPython and Arduino-C++ subsets run by the interpreter with the Pico pin map.
models.2: Digital I/O on GP0 to GP22 and GP26 to GP28, PWM and interrupts on every GPIO.
models.3: 12-bit analog reads on GP26 to GP28, returned as 0 to 65535 by read_u16(), I2C master on GP4 and GP5, serial output and the on-board LED on GP25.

not.1: The PIO state machines and the second core.
not.2: The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radio of the W boards.
not.3: The RP2350 differences beyond the pin map, and the flash and power-supply behaviour.

gap: undefined No electrical ratings are listed yet, so no pin-overload check exists for this board.
